title: A Quantitative Analysis and Guidelines of Data Streaming Accelerator in Modern Intel Xeon Scalable Processors
problem: Data movement operations in memory are a significant bottleneck in datacenter workloads, and semiconductor power density constraints require specialized accelerators to continue scaling performance beyond traditional CPU scaling.
motivation: As power density plateaus with technology scaling, specialized on-chip data accelerators are needed to improve both performance and energy efficiency for datacenter applications.
method: The paper performs a comprehensive evaluation of Intel's Data Streaming Accelerator (DSA) integrated in Sapphire Rapids processors through microbenchmarks and real datacenter workloads, analyzing its support for data movement, CRC32, delta computations, and data integrity operations. The evaluation includes analysis of DSA characteristics, software ecosystem, and practical guidelines validated through a DPDK Vhost case study.
key_novelty: Comprehensive quantitative analysis with practical programming guidelines for optimizing specialized data streaming accelerators in modern processors.
contributions: Comprehensive quantitative evaluation of DSA throughput benefits across microbenchmarks and real datacenter workloads
Analysis of DSA architectural characteristics and software ecosystem
Practical programming guidelines for effective DSA utilization
Case study demonstrating DSA optimization in DPDK Vhost applications

metrics.speedup: throughput improvements over CPU software baseline

primary_theme: Hardware acceleration for datacenter data movement optimization
